text.p: Contract miner and civil engineer Henry Walker Group Ltd is currently looking at 10 percent growth in revenue for both 1997/98 and 1998/99, managing director Richard Ryan said on Wednesday.
However, Ryan told Reuters he would not be surprised if profit margins came under pressure from increasing competition in the contracting industry.
"I really believe for the next two years we can see quite adequate work (to meet revenue targets)," he said.
"It is really a question of whether or not there will be pressure on the margins which of course will affect our level of profitability," he said of the company's continuing outlook.
Asked if Henry Walker would target 10 percent growth in revenue in 1998/99 to June 30 as well as in the current financial year, Ryan said: "Yes, at this stage."
The company, which earlier announced a 1996/97 net profit rise of 18 percent to A$20.9 million, is also targeting a 10 percent rise in earnings for 1997/98.
Henry Walker had a record A$1 billion in work on hand at June 30, 22 percent higher than the previous year, with A$300 million work on hand for the 1997/98 year.
Ryan said the company would be bidding for several iron ore contracts to be offered by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd in Western Australia during 1997/98 and hoped to win some work in South Australia.
With only around nine percent of gross revenue exposed to the gold industry, he said he was not concerned about the impact of the price slump for bullion on the company.

Ryan said the company was in the advanced stages of considering a small acquisition for its troubled transport services division, and also planned to sell off a portion of the business, although he could not give further details.
"If we can sell it off and replace it with what we want to, it should improve our bottom line in that section," he said.
Profit before tax for transport services dropped to A$2.6 million in 1996/97, compared to A$3.1 million the year before.
Ryan said he did not expect Henry Walker's Indonesian operation to improve significantly in 1997/98 but the company would maintain its presence there.
